questions.question: In which village was Guru Amar Das Ji born?
questions.explanation: Guru Amar Das Ji was born at Basarke, a village in present-day Amritsar district, into a Bhalla Khatri family.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia – Amar Das, Guru

questions.question: Before becoming a Sikh, Amar Das was known for making many pilgrimages to which holy place?
questions.explanation: As a devout Vaishnav, Amar Das made regular pilgrimages to Haridwar — chroniclers record twenty — before he found his Guru.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia – Amar Das, Guru

questions.question: Whose singing of Guru Nanak Dev Ji's bani led Amar Das to Guru Angad Dev Ji?
options: Bibi Amro Ji, Guru Angad Dev Ji's daughter
questions.explanation: Amar Das heard Bibi Amro, daughter of Guru Angad Dev Ji (married into his family), singing Guru Nanak's bani; she took him to her father at Khadur.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia – Amar Das, Guru

questions.question: What service is Guru Amar Das Ji especially remembered for performing for Guru Angad Dev Ji?
options: Bringing water from the River Beas
questions.explanation: For about twelve years Amar Das served Guru Angad Dev Ji, famously bringing water from the River Beas even on a stormy night.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia – Amar Das, Guru

questions.question: When a weaver woman mocked the stumbling Amar Das as 'Amaru Nithavan' (homeless), what did Guru Angad Dev Ji call him?
questions.explanation: After Amar Das stumbled over a weaver's peg on a dark night, Guru Angad Dev Ji praised his devotion and called him the home of the homeless; Gurdwara Khaddi (Killa) Sahib marks the spot.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia – Amar Das, Guru

questions.question: At about what age did Guru Amar Das Ji become Guru?
questions.explanation: Guru Amar Das Ji became the third Guru in 1552 at the age of 73, showing that devotion and service know no age.
questions.source: Sikhs.org – Guru Amar Das
questions.note: Based on the widely accepted birth year 1479; a minority source gives 1509.

questions.question: Which town did Guru Amar Das Ji make the centre of the Sikh faith?
questions.explanation: Guru Amar Das Ji made Goindwal, on the Beas at a major ferry crossing, his headquarters.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia – Amar Das, Guru

questions.question: How many steps lead down to the water in the Baoli Sahib built by Guru Amar Das Ji at Goindwal?
questions.explanation: The baoli (stepwell) at Goindwal, begun by Guru Amar Das Ji in 1559, has 84 steps leading down to the water.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Goindval

questions.question: Goindwal is named after whom?
options: Goinda, a local trader who planned the settlement
A Mughal governor named Gobind Khan
A Sufi saint named Goinda Shah
questions.explanation: Goindwal is named after Goinda (Gonda), a Marvaha Khatri trader whose settlement plan was completed with Amar Das's help at Guru Angad Dev Ji's instruction.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Goindval

questions.question: Who, out of jealousy, kicked Guru Amar Das Ji off his seat at Goindwal?
options: Sri Chand, son of Guru Nanak Dev Ji
Datu, son of Guru Angad Dev Ji
questions.explanation: Datu, Guru Angad Dev Ji's son, kicked Guru Amar Das Ji from his seat; the Guru humbly replied by asking whether his old bones had hurt Datu's foot, and withdrew to Basarke.
questions.source: Sikhs.org – Guru Amar Das

questions.question: How many manjis (preaching districts) did Guru Amar Das Ji establish?
questions.explanation: Guru Amar Das Ji organised the Sikh sangats into 22 manjis, each under a devout Sikh who preached the Gurus' message.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Manji

questions.question: What is the literal meaning of 'manji', the word used for Guru Amar Das Ji's preaching districts?
questions.explanation: In Punjabi 'manji' means a simple string cot; the appointed preachers sat on such raised seats while teaching.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Manji

questions.question: What does the principle 'Pehle Pangat, Pichhon Sangat' associated with Guru Amar Das Ji mean?
options: Eat together in the langar first, then join the Guru's company
Serve the elders before the young
questions.explanation: Guru Amar Das Ji required every visitor, whatever their rank or caste, to first eat in the langar pangat before meeting him.
questions.source: Sikh Missionary Society – Pangat

questions.question: Which Mughal emperor sat and ate in the langar before meeting Guru Amar Das Ji at Goindwal?
questions.explanation: Emperor Akbar visited Goindwal and, like every pilgrim, ate in the langar before meeting Guru Amar Das Ji.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia – Amar Das, Guru

questions.question: How did Guru Amar Das Ji respond when Akbar offered revenue from villages to support the langar?
options: He accepted and built a fort
He accepted it for the poor of Lahore
He declined, saying the langar should run on the offerings of the Sangat
questions.explanation: Guru Amar Das Ji declined Akbar's grant, holding that the langar must rely on voluntary offerings and the labour of the Sikhs.
questions.source: Sikhs.org – Guru Amar Das
questions.note: Some accounts say the grant was later given to Bibi Bhani; only the Guru's refusal is asked.

questions.question: In which raag did Guru Amar Das Ji compose Anand Sahib?
questions.explanation: Anand Sahib, composed by Guru Amar Das Ji in forty pauris, is in Raag Ramkali; its shortened form is recited at the end of congregational services and ceremonies.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Anandu

questions.question: According to tradition, who was named 'Anand' after Guru Amar Das Ji completed the Anand Sahib?
options: His newborn grandson, son of Baba Mohri
A Sikh preacher of a manji
questions.explanation: Tradition says Guru Amar Das Ji had just completed the composition when news came of the birth of a grandson (son of Mohri), who was named Anand.
questions.source: Encyclopaedia of Sikhism (Punjabi University) – Anandu

questions.question: Which social practices did Guru Amar Das Ji speak out against?
questions.explanation: Guru Amar Das Ji opposed sati (widow-burning) and discouraged purdah (veiling of women), and gave women roles in leading sangats.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia – Amar Das, Guru

questions.question: Guru Amar Das Ji designated which occasions for Sikhs to gather at Goindwal?
questions.explanation: Guru Amar Das Ji set the beginning of Baisakh and Magh, and Diwali, as days for Sikhs to assemble at Goindwal.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia – Amar Das, Guru

questions.question: Whom did Guru Amar Das Ji choose as his successor?
options: Bhai Jetha Ji, his son-in-law, who became Guru Ram Das Ji
questions.explanation: Guru Amar Das Ji chose Bhai Jetha, husband of his daughter Bibi Bhani, who became Guru Ram Das Ji in 1574.
questions.source: The Sikh Encyclopedia – Amar Das, Guru
